title: The Portrait of the Fens
premise: When a drowned woman is pulled from the Fens wearing Oscar Kavanagh's own missing coat and scarf, the night dispatcher becomes both suspect and witness in a case the police can't crack — because every detail matches a twenty-year-old unsolved drowning that was never in any public file. Oscar realizes the killer is someone who has read the original case file: a cop, a clerk, or a family member of the first victim, and that the thefts from their closet were staged to frame them. As Oscar and the first victim's estranged daughter, Maren, dig into a legacy of land fraud and a found-family of misfits who once protected each other with silence, they set a trap using a falsified 'new evidence' file as bait. In the climax at the drainage station where both women died, the killer — the retired evidence clerk who has spent two decades guarding the secret out of twisted loyalty — is exposed, and Oscar must choose between the truth that clears their name and protecting the surrogate family that kept the original lie alive.
about_author: Ulyana Sterling is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing testimony in cases that never made the evening news. She writes mysteries from a houseboat on the edge of the wetlands, where the fog arrives on schedule and the water keeps its secrets.

chapters.title: The Coat You Lent the Dead
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. During a rain-soaked night shift, Oscar dispatches a cab to the Fens and later identifies the recovered body's clothing as items stolen from their own closet weeks ago. Detective Ilori treats them as suspect, not witness. Emotional beat: the vertigo of being written into a stranger's death, and the first flicker of recognition that the scene mirrors an old, sealed case.

chapters.title: What the File Forgets
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, with an interlude in Maren's. Oscar and Maren — the 2003 victim's daughter, who grew up on rumors instead of answers — compare notes and discover the new crime scene replicates details that exist only in the sealed case file. Emotional beat: two lonely people recognizing each other as family of a kind, bound by the same dead woman's silence.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Locked Room
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The pair trace the old case to a found-family of night workers who covered for one another about land fraud at the drainage station. When Oscar's apartment is searched and a planted 'trophy' surfaces, Maren realizes the killer is inside the circle — someone who loved the group enough to kill for its secret. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into dread as every ally becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: The Statute and the Water
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. With hours before the statute expires, Oscar and Maren seed a fake evidence file naming the true heir and wait at the drainage station. The retired evidence clerk comes to destroy it, confessing he protected the family out of loyalty. Oscar chooses truth over the group's fragile peace; the confession is recorded, the frame dissolved, and Oscar and Maren leave as the only family either has left. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into belonging.
